# Zero strict JPEG scan completion backport

Base: the complete production source and unchanged Cargo manifests/readme/licenses from the crates.io zune-jpeg 0.5.15 archive. No decoder/version switch, new transitive dependency, arithmetic coding, streaming API or custom JPEG parser. Base archive and every copied file SHA-256 are recorded in SOURCE.json; licenses remain MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR Zlib.

Correction reference: Chromium rust mirror commit `efee7ad5ea0225a78223f51cfc8fae7a82f67263`, `chromium_crates_io/vendor/zune-jpeg-v0_5/src/bitstream.rs` (Git blob `9abe0be522e375722dc2fba6d2b71327df679cb2`). Pinned files and SHA-256 are in SOURCE.json. Source URL: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/third_party/rust/+/efee7ad5ea0225a78223f51cfc8fae7a82f67263/chromium_crates_io/vendor/zune-jpeg-v0_5/src/bitstream.rs

The fork is much broader than this correction, so the initial backport adapted only the `marker_bits`/`insufficient_data` fields, `consume_marker_bits` function and its drop_bits/get_bits/refill/reset hooks are adapted. These count real buffered entropy bits before a latched marker separately from decoder-generated zero lookahead. Reading ahead into a marker is permitted; consuming synthetic bits is a truncated scan. The exact base-to-vendor source diff is strict-completion.patch.

Integration adaptations for the older decoder: it has no BitStream trait or strict flag. Its callers already own DecoderOptions, so `check_scan_complete(strict)` rejects the latched insufficient-data flag only in strict mode. Baseline checks before marker handling can consume/reset the flag; progressive checks after every MCU before restart handling can reset it. Reset clears the counter/flag at scan/restart boundaries. Initial marker detection snapshots bits_left before EOI adds its synthetic byte. Later synthetic refills never add real entropy credit. Both constructors initialize the state. No lenient error/output policy changes.

The direct exact-version dependency allows host validation to request strict RGB decode into one checked output buffer. The image crate continues using its own lenient option unchanged. Host limits reject originals >25 MiB and dimensions >40 million pixels before full decode, check output allocation <=160 million bytes, and bound PNG through ImageReader limits. This does not claim that the decoder's internal progressive coefficient/scratch buffers are included in that output-buffer budget; their size is bounded by the admitted dimensions and supported JPEG component/sampling limits.

Regression evidence lives under build/core-market/evidence/2026-11-16/task-paper-media-jpeg-*. Tests use synthetic RGB/grayscale/baseline/progressive/restart controls, first/later scan entropy cuts with EOI, unchanged original hashes/bytes, PNG/size/dimension controls and the legacy lenient image wrapper. No real user media.

Update policy: remove this patch only after a released upstream decoder passes these strict-completeness regressions. Re-audit the exact transplant and regenerate SOURCE.json/strict-completion.patch when updating the base. Do not import the complete Chromium fork.

## Round2: required baseline MCU and component coverage

The entropy-bit counter alone did not establish completeness: the older decoder can dispatch COM/APP/SOS after an early row and then leave the scan before synthetic bits are consumed. The strict baseline path now keeps a non-RST marker latched while required rows remain. It consumes every MCU in each row (the lenient early-row-break remains unchanged); real buffered lookahead can legitimately serve later rows, so seeing a marker is not itself an error. Consuming synthetic bits still fails through the original backport. Only after all required rows can strict marker dispatch exit/reset a scan.

The current scan's component IDs are captured before decoding, since SOS parsing may replace z_order. Components are marked complete only after the final required row; strict image success requires every frame component complete. Repeated component scans and extra SOS after a complete interleaved scan fail. This adapts the pinned Chromium decoder.rs `mark_baseline_scan_components_complete` and scan-component snapshot idea into a local stack bitset, without importing persistent scan/checkpoint machinery. The added upstream decoder.rs hash is in SOURCE.json. The strict-only deferral is a compatibility adaptation to the older MCU loop, not a verbatim complete-fork transplant.

Supported geometry boundary: baseline RGB/grayscale, progressive and sequential component scans with 1x1 sampling retain their controls, including real restart markers. The base version incorrectly decodes subsampled sequential component geometry (e.g. generated valid 4:2:0 component scans). Strict mode rejects that geometry explicitly; lenient policy remains unchanged. This avoids publishing corrupted success without adding a geometry decoder fork. The claim is completeness of supported JPEG decoding, not universal JPEG conformance.

Round2 regressions include exact early-COM prefix2241, APP13 and SOS transitions at multiple entropy cuts through both cache and shared validation, complete COM/APP13 controls, missing sequential components, sequential1x1+RST controls, a skinny grayscale image retaining real entropy across lookahead rows, explicit unsupported-valid-geometry refusal and prior baseline/progressive/plain-EOI/PNG/bounds/preview coverage.
